lead.tldr: Bitcoin ETFs record $225 million inflows led by BlackRock IBIT signaling institutional demand resilience. • Visa and Stripe expand stablecoin cards to over 100 countries boosting global payment adoption. • Indiana legalizes crypto in state retirement plans opening new institutional investment channels. • BitGo rolls out MiCA-compliant services across 30 EEA countries aiding European regulatory integration. • CZ-backed YZi Labs commits $100 million to BNB fund enhancing structured institutional access. • Middle East tensions trigger global market plunge highlighting crypto macro vulnerability risks.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, As institutional adoption accelerates with Bitcoin ETFs drawing record inflows and stablecoin payments expanding to 100+ countries, Web3 infrastructure faces mounting security challenges from geopolitical threats and regulatory scrutiny. Blockwall remains committed to backing the founders building resilient, compliant solutions that will power the decentralized economy through this pivotal moment.

top_signals.title: Iran’s revenge: drones damage data centers for Amazon Web Services, reveal west’s Achilles Heel
top_signals.summary: Drone strikes damaged multiple Amazon Web Services data centers across the Middle East, with two facilities in the United Arab Emirates directly struck and another site in Bahrain sustaining infrastructure damage during retaliatory Iranian military operations following Operation Epic Fury. The attacks disrupted power systems and caused structural damage that impaired two of three data center sites in AWS's UAE region, forcing the company to urge customers to activate disaster recovery plans and migrate critical workloads out of the region. This incident marks the first publicly confirmed case of a hyperscale U.S. commercial data center being physically affected in real-world combat, demonstrating how precision drone technology has made critical digital infrastructure vulnerable in geopolitically contested regions. For institutional investors, the attack underscores systemic risks to cloud service providers operating in volatile regions and raises questions about the resilience of distributed infrastructure models that underpin global digital economies.

top_signals.title: South Korea Halts Trading as Global Markets Plunge
top_signals.summary: South Korea halted trading due to a stock market plunge. The selloff was triggered by escalating conflict in the Middle East, impacting global markets.

top_signals.title: Ex-LAPD Cop Convicted of $350K Crypto Theft
top_signals.summary: A former LAPD officer was convicted of stealing $350,000 in Bitcoin from a 17-year-old boy by force. The officer faces sentencing on March 31.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $225M Inflows Led by BlackRock's IBIT
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin ETFs experienced $225 million in net inflows, primarily driven by BlackRock's IBIT. Ether ETFs saw modest outflows, indicating cautious investor sentiment towards Ethereum.

top_signals.title: Visa and Stripe plan global expansion of stablecoin card issuance product to over 100 countries
top_signals.summary: Visa and Stripe are planning a global expansion of their stablecoin card issuance product to over 100 countries, initially focused on Central and South America. The product is currently live in 18 countries.

top_signals.title: CZ–backed YZi Labs invests $100 million into Hash Global's BNB fund
top_signals.summary: YZi Labs, backed by CZ, has invested $100 million into Hash Global's BNB fund. This investment allows institutions to allocate BNB through a structured, institutional-grade product.

top_signals.title: Visa and Stripe's Bridge to Expand Stablecoin Cards to 100+ Countries
top_signals.summary: Visa and Bridge are expanding their stablecoin-linked card product to over 100 countries by the end of the year, significantly increasing the accessibility of stablecoin payments. The cards will be accepted at 175 million merchant locations.

top_signals.title: Indiana to enact bill allowing crypto investments in retirement plans after governor's sign-off
top_signals.summary: Indiana Governor Mike Braun signed House Bill 1042 into law, permitting certain state retirement programs to include crypto investments. This makes Indiana one of the first states to allow crypto exposure in retirement plans.

top_signals.title: Digital Finance Could Deliver $17 Billion Annual Boost for Australia
top_signals.summary: A report by the Digital Finance Cooperative Research Centre suggests that Australia could gain $17 billion annually by advancing tokenized markets and digital assets. However, this potential will not be realized under the current trajectory.

top_signals.title: Visa expands stablecoin settlement pilot as Bridge targets 100-country card rollout
top_signals.summary: Visa is expanding its stablecoin settlement pilot program through Bridge. Bridge is targeting a 100-country card rollout.

top_signals.title: BitGo Launches MiCA-Compliant Crypto-as-a-Service Across 30 EEA Countries
top_signals.summary: BitGo Europe GmbH has launched its MiCA-compliant Crypto-as-a-Service across the EEA, allowing banks and fintechs to integrate regulated custody, trading, and SEPA on/off-ramps through APIs. This move signifies BitGo's commitment to regulatory compliance and expands its service offerings within the European market.

top_signals.title: TD Cowen says banks likely to lose stablecoin yield fight, but prolonged dispute could put crypto bill at risk
top_signals.summary: TD Cowen suggests banks are likely to lose the political battle over stablecoin yields, arguing against consumers benefiting from them. However, the prolonged dispute could jeopardize the passage of a crypto bill.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Today's headlines underscore just how deeply intertwined crypto, geopolitics, and traditional finance have become. Iranian drone strikes damaged Amazon Web Services data centers in the UAE and Bahrain, marking the first confirmed physical attack on hyperscale cloud infrastructure in a live conflict. Meanwhile, Bitcoin ETFs recorded $225 million in net inflows led by BlackRock's IBIT, demonstrating institutional demand resilience even as South Korea halted equity trading amid global market turmoil. On the payments front, Visa and Stripe announced plans to expand stablecoin-linked card issuance to over 100 countries, with acceptance at 175 million merchant locations. BitGo launched MiCA-compliant Crypto-as-a-Service across 30 EEA countries, and Indiana became one of the first U.S. states to allow crypto investments in state retirement plans. At Blockwall, Europe's leading Web3 venture capital firm, we see these developments as validation of our thesis: institutional infrastructure and regulatory clarity are the catalysts that will drive the next wave of adoption. Our portfolio companies like Spiko's tokenized money market funds and Validation Cloud's enterprise node infrastructure are positioned at the intersection of these trends.
